s: Which part of the constitution of India declares the ideals of the welfare state?
x: Articles 36 to 51 of the Indian Constitution outline the Directive Principles of State Policy, which serve as guidelines for the state (non-justiciable) in its pursuit of establishing a welfare state focused on social and economic justice. Additionally, they advocate for the creation of a social order where justice is integral to all institutions and practices within the nation.

x: 'Equal Pay for Equal Work for both men and women' (Article 39(d)) and the Uniform Civil Code (Article 44) are listed among the Directive Principles in Part IV of the Constitution of India. Fundamental Duties *The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR. *These were added on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. *This amendment added a new part (Part IV A) which consists of only one article, that is, Article 51 A. *Presently, the number of Fundamental Duties, as per the Article 51 A, is 11, whereas originally, at the time of its inclusion in the Constitution, the number was 10. The 11th Fundamental Duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. *According to Article 51 A, it shall be the duty of every citizen of India – (a) To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem; (b) To cherish and follow the noble ideas which inspired our national struggle for freedom; (c) To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity
